finding: Every request re-did work that never changes (path joins, build keys, a URL object and a Headers object, a session-key HMAC, two manifest reads from disk)
evidence: Five commits on perf/backend-speed (CHANGELOG 0.3.5). Interleaved A/B on one machine: +15% JSON list, +32% authenticated GET, +21% POST, +41% pre-rendered page, +23% server-rendered page; form POST 32,000 to 80,000 req/s in the full run (benchmarks/results/before-after.md, ab-published-vs-final.txt)

finding: Devora.js API routes are behind Fastify, Hono and NestJS on Fastify on every JSON scenario
evidence: Published 0.3.5, medians: JSON list 4th of 10 (26% below the leader), authenticated GET 6th (43% below), POST valid 5th (39%) and invalid 4th (36%); on POST it is level with Express (ranges overlap). Part of the gap is not in the framework (the same JSON.stringify runs in every app, about half of the list scenario); the rest is per-request work the bare frameworks do not do (security headers, a request context with session and CSRF methods, a real session lookup). benchmarks/results/backend-report.md

finding: The built-in memory session store clones each record on every read (structuredClone, about 8% of an authenticated request)
evidence: CPU profile of the authenticated scenario. Not changed: the clone keeps a handler from mutating the stored record; a cheaper copy needs a decision on that behavior.

finding: Memory after load is higher than the bare backend frameworks
evidence: Published 0.3.5: Devora.js 285 MB after the API scenarios against 167 to 258 MB for Express, Fastify and both NestJS platforms (Hono 222 MB; Next.js, SvelteKit, React Router and Astro are higher, 329 to 600 MB). A faster server also keeps more heap, so this is not proof of a leak; the 10-minute soak on the 0.3.5 code held steady (about 314 MB, +3 MB between the halves of the run).

finding: ws on the same port as devora start
evidence: Works through a wrapper script that calls createNodeServer (the function the CLI calls; a public, documented export of @devorajs/adapter-node that returns the http.Server) and handles upgrade itself: bad token 401, good token connected and echoed, API and security headers unchanged on the same port. Plain devora start exposes no server and no hook. Smallest core change: an onServer(server) option. Guide: Live updates (WebSockets).

finding: Server-sent events from an API route
evidence: A string body is sent complete after the handler finishes (first byte at 1.5 s for three events 0.5 s apart, then the connection closes, so an EventSource reconnects in a loop); a ReadableStream, an async iterable or a Readable as the body answers 500. Smallest core change: let sendApiResponse pipe a stream or async iterable and destroy it when the client disconnects.

finding: Socket.IO as a separate server (examples/realtime)
evidence: Run from a scratch copy on the published 0.3.4 packages: all 19 checks of examples/check.mjs pass. Not tested in a browser.

finding: Background jobs: BullMQ with Redis and a separate worker
evidence: Tested on one Node server: an authenticated route enqueued (202), the worker ran it, the route returned completed in about 330 ms; unauthenticated enqueue is 401. bullmq needs ioredis installed separately. In CI as examples/background-jobs (the Redis part skips when there is no Redis). Guide: Background jobs.

finding: Background jobs without Redis: a SQLite queue and a worker
evidence: node:sqlite: result in about 100 to 220 ms. One server only (both processes share the file). In CI as examples/background-jobs, always run.

finding: node-cron inside devora start
evidence: Works, but there is no start-up hook: the schedule registers when the route that contains it is first imported (at its first request).

finding: Each of the above on Vercel or Netlify
evidence: Not deployed, so not verified. Expected from the platforms' documented model, not tested: WebSockets, long-lived timers and a SQLite file on a function's disk do not fit functions; a BullMQ worker must run elsewhere.

finding: A fresh scaffold prints npm warn Unknown project config "link-workspace-packages" on every npm command
evidence: Source: packages/scaffold/src/scaffoldProjectFiles.ts:137 writes a project .npmrc containing link-workspace-packages=true, a pnpm setting (pnpm needs it so the plain "*" workspace dependencies link locally instead of being fetched from the registry). npm 11 does not know it and warns, saying it will stop working in the next major version. Verified: in a scaffold, npm config get registry warns with the .npmrc in place and is silent with it moved away. The repo root and every example carry the same file. Not fixed.

finding: On newer npm, install prints an allow-scripts warning for esbuild's postinstall
evidence: Reproduced with npm 11.17.0 in an empty project: npm install esbuild@0.25.12 prints "1 package has install scripts not yet covered by allowScripts: esbuild@0.25.12 (postinstall: node install.js)". esbuild comes in through Vite. Install, devora dev and devora build still work. The warning comes from npm, not from Devora.js code; getting-started says so in one line. Not fixed.

finding: A fresh project did not install with pnpm 11 or later (tried 12.10)
evidence: pnpm 11 and later ignore link-workspace-packages in .npmrc (ERR_PNPM_FETCH_404 for @devorajs/backend, then ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS). The 0.4.0 scaffold writes linkWorkspacePackages: true and allowBuilds: esbuild: true into pnpm-workspace.yaml; a new project passed create, install, dev, build, start, add, a package script and the one-off command on pnpm 9.15, 10.34 and 12.10, Node 20 and 22. Projects made by create-devora 0.3.x still need the two keys added by hand (Getting started).

finding: A fresh project did not run under Yarn 4's default Plug'n'Play linker
evidence: Install succeeded, then devora dev and build stopped with "@devorajs/cli tried to access esbuild". The 0.4.0 scaffold writes .yarnrc.yml with nodeLinker: node-modules when the package manager is Yarn; a new project passed the same steps on Yarn 4.18 (default settings) and Yarn 1.22, Node 20 and 22. Projects made by 0.3.x need the file added by hand (Getting started).
